title: getNumPartitions() and spark_partition_id() returning different values
question:
I have a dataframe with only 3 rows. When I call df.rdd.getNumPartitions() ot gives me 8. But when I do:

df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()).groupBy("partition_id").count().display()

It gives me 3 partitions with one row each. I am confused as to why this is happening.

Then environment I am using is Databricks Community Edition (Cluster has 1 executor with 2 cores)

The code to create dataframe:

data = [(1, "Alice", 25), (2, "Bob", 40), (3, "Charlie", 65)]
df=spark.createDataFrame(data,['Id','Name','Age'])

from pyspark.sql.functions import spark_partition_id

df.withColumn("partition_id", spark_partition_id()).groupBy("partition_id").count().display()
answer:
getNumPartitions() will show how many partitions that Spark currently has regardless of whether any data is in the partition or not.

If you run this, you will see all partitions with where each row data is located.

df.withColumn("partition_id", F.spark_partition_id()).rdd.glom().collect()

For me, it shows this. You can see 8 elements in the array which is 8 partitions total. Only 3 partitions have data and 5 are empty partitions.

[[],
 [],
 [Row(Id=1, Name='Alice', Age=25, partition_id=2)],
 [],
 [],
 [Row(Id=2, Name='Bob', Age=40, partition_id=5)],
 [],
 [Row(Id=3, Name='Charlie', Age=65, partition_id=7)]]

If interested, you can try playing with partitionBy and see how Pyspark partition a certain data. (reference link)
